Photograph: Bianca de Marchi/AAP View image in fullscreen Damien Tudehope (right) has not been named as a person of interest in Operation Rosny but has stood down as shadow attorney general. Photograph: Bianca de Marchi/AAP Independent Commission Against Corruption Analysis ‘Did you send that report?’ The Icac bombshell that came late for Damien Tudehope Anne Davies The former Liberal finance minister was questioned by Icac counsel assisting, Peggy Dwyer, on Tuesday Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Tue 4 Aug 2026 11.00 EDT Last modified on Tue 4 Aug 2026 11.02 EDT Share The bombshell came in the last five minutes of former finance minister and rightwing powerbroker Damien Tudehope’s examination before the Independent Commission Against Corruption . At 3.30pm on Tuesday, Tudehope was shown an email which he sent in February 2023, attaching a leaked draft parliamentary report into branch stacking in the Hills area by the Reformers, the shadowy group at the centre of Icac’s Operation Rosny. It has probably imperilled his parliamentary career. “Would you regard yourself … as being bound by keeping it confidential?” asked counsel assisting, Peggy Dwyer, SC. Tudehope visibly tensed. “Did you send that report in draft to Mr Greenwood?” she asked, showing him the email. “It appears that I did,” Tudehope replied quietly. Jeremy Greenwood is one of the group of conservative Catholic men who set up the Reformers, recruiting like-minded conservatives to the Liberal party in order to take over branches from the moderate and centre-right factions. In 2023, during the parliamentary inquiry, the key Reformers and associates – Christian Ellis, the then premier’s brothers Jean-Claude Perrottet and Charles Perrottet, and Greenwood – had left NSW to avoid being called to the parliamentary inquiry. NSW Liberal admits to leaking confidential report to young conservative powerbrokers, inquiry hears Read more Tudehope told Icac he had had a conversation with the premier, Dom Perrottet, who said he knew his brother had gone to Fiji. Leaking a draft parliamentary report is a serious breach of parliamentary rules and contempt of parliament. It may even constitute corrupt conduct depending on the motivation of the leak. Tudehope has not been named as a person of interest in Operation Rosny but has stood down as shadow attorney general. Wednesday’s evidence, however, raised questions of just how tightly Tudehope was tied into the activities of the Reformers and the donations they are alleged to have taken to fund their branch takeover activities. The day started well enough. A politician for 20 years, Tudehope was happy to talk expansively about his alignment with the Reformers’ causes on conservative social issues. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email He’d been happy to be a speaker at events advocating for safe schools and opposing gender fluidity and marriage equality. But when it came to questions about whether funds flowing into the Reformers were political in nature, the lawyer in Tudehope emerged. “I don’t necessarily accept the premise that every event where someone signs up to a party as a result of attending the event is necessarily a contribution for the benefit of a party, and I think I identified to you that there are people who may sign up to a party to provide no benefit to a party,” Tudehope said. “So, to the extent that you identify for the benefit of a party, I think that’s a very moot point about the definition of a benefit to the Liberal party.” Dwyer wasn’t letting him off the hook so easily. In painstaking detail, she ran him through text messages and WhatsApp groups that she alleged showed knowledge of the secret money trail. Tudehope’s close friend and former law partner Michael O’Hara, who became a successful hotelier, became a major donor to the Reformers, giving $165,000 to a number of entities after introductions at a function at Tudehope’s home where the News Corp columnist Miranda Devine was the speaker. Tudehope agreed he might have introduced Ellis to O’Hara, but denied he had encouraged illegal donations. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks Preview latest after newsletter promotion “If you think that I would expose a friend of mine to that level of scrutiny that he was exposed to, 83 years of age with stage three/four cancer, you think that I would have done that in circumstances where I knew that he would be a prohibited donor for the purposes of the Electoral Funding Act, not on your life!” he said. Under sustained questioning, Tudehope agreed that using invoices to public relations firms to channel payments was “concealment” as the commissioner, Fabian Gleeson, phrased it. The other major backer of the Reformers was Catholic Schools NSW and here Tudehope has several connections. He was friends with the CEO, Dallas McInerney, also a powerful key figure in the right, while his son James worked in communications at Catholic Schools NSW. Icac heard on Wednesday that at a Sunday lunch, James Tudehope told his father he was being pressured to pay an invoice from Ellis. He was “very agitated” because he didn’t think they were getting value for money, Damien Tudehope said. Tudehope said he recommended his son take it up with McInerney, his boss. In Dwyer’s opening address we learned that Ellis, who has moved to London and declined to appear, had used his public relations firm, Beckington, to take donations for Reformer work. Tudehope was also an employer of key Reformers in his ministerial office. In August 2019, the federal member for Berowra, Julian Leeser, who was unaligned to a faction, went public with his concerns about the branch stacking in the Hills in the Sydney Morning Herald. Icac heard that Ellis had said publicly at a Reformers event that “Leeser was a lefty and had to go”, drawing the ire of several in the party. Dwyer tabled an article by Tom Rabe written in 2019 about the factional war and the involvement of two of the Reformers, Ellis and Jean-Claude Perrottet, who were employed in Tudehope’s office. He suggested Liberals were concerned the pair spent most of their time on branch stacking. By October 2019, Tudehope’s office let Ellis go, concerned about the adverse publicity his activities were drawing. Tudehope said it was the chief of staff who made the call. By 2020, the heat on the Reformers was increasing. Tudehope was on Tuesday shown messages from 2020 between members of the Reformers in which they said MPs “were getting scared about ICAC,” and that “Scott and Damien are afraid”. Tudehope denied knowing what they were about. But by the end of the day, he could have little doubt he now had reasons to fear Icac. Beállítom Kigyulladt a száraz fű hétfőn délután Tapolca külterületén, a 77-es főút közelében – írja a Veol . A lap szerint a lángok háromszáz méter hosszan egy fenyőerdőbe is belekaptak, és azok lombkoronája is égni kezdett, a helyszínre pedig nagy erőkkel vonultak ki a tűzoltók. A lángok több kertet, egy lakóautót, egy melléképületet, egy lovardát, egy napelemparkot, egy szeméttelepet, sőt több lakóépületet is megközelítettek. A fenyőerdőnél a tűz tízméteres lángokkal és hatalmas füsttel égett, ami miatt egy időre le kellett zárni a forgalmat a 77-es úton. A tüzet három vármegyéből, az ajkai, a badacsonytomaji, a keszthelyi, a pápai, a sárvári és a veszprémi hivatásos, a tapolcai önkormányzati, valamint a tapolcai, a nagyvázsonyi, a tótvázsonyi, a köveskáli, a kővágóörsi, a monostorapáti, a balatonfüredi, a taliándörögdi, a gógánfai és a zalahalápi-sáskai önkéntes tűzoltók oltják a katasztrófavédelmi műveleti szolgálat irányítása mellett. A tűzoltók drónnal légi felderítést is végeznek – írja az MTI. A honvédség négy vízszállító járművel és két helikopterrel szállt be a mentésbe, amelyet civilek lajtoskocsikkal segítenek – mondta el a Telexnek Csondor Henrietta, a Veszprém Vármegyei Katasztrófavédelmi Igazgatóság szóvivője. Az oltást a változó irányból fújó nagyon intenzív szél nehezítette. Este fél nyolckor telefonon érdeklődtünk a katasztrófavédelemnél, hogy hogy állnak az oltással. Csondor Henrietta szóvivő kérdésünkre azt mondta, hogy a tüzet addigra munkagépekkel körülszántották, vagyis sikerült úgy lokalizálni, hogy ne tudjon továbbterjedni. Tájékoztatása szerint a lángok összesen 40 hektárt érintettek. A 77-es főúton mostanra már újraindították az autóforgalmat. https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/24/at-l.text: A hack of Russia's federal statistics agency Rosstat has revealed that at least 490,000 Russian military personnel have been killed in Ukraine since the start of Moscow's full-scale invasion in February 2022, according to data obtained by hackers and analysed by multiple independent news outlets.Two hacking groups, Cyber Partisans of Belarus and Silent Crow — which also carried out a 2025 attack on Aeroflot's servers — extracted the data in a breach on the night of 1 November.The hackers accessed Rosstat's electronic document management system and database, which contains around 23 terabytes of statistical, economic and personal data, including census materials.The figure of at least 490,000 deaths derives from official death certificates registered between February 2022 and the end of August 2026.Meduza, applying actuarial and epidemiological modelling to the data, estimated at least 720,000 irrecoverable losses when it includes those missing in action. Rosstat's documents alone cannot capture the full toll, as the database does not include servicemen whose deaths have not yet been registered.Researchers and journalists justify including the missing in total loss figures because, according to Mediazona, confirmed survival is recorded in fewer than 10% of missing servicemen cases.Under current battlefield conditions, with drone warfare making the evacuation of bodies increasingly difficult, the death tally is likely to grow.Deaths are also registered with an average delay of 3.5 months, and those of missing soldiers with a delay of about a year, Novaya Evropa reported.Using the conservative estimate of 490,000 to 500,000 dead, Russia sustained an average of 280 to 300 fatalities a day — one death every five minutes — according to Important Stories, which examined the leak alongside more than a dozen other independent outlets.The outlet found that 92% of Russian servicemen died from explosions and shrapnel, with firearms accounting for only 1.3% of deaths. The Insider identified more than 370,000 of the dead by name.The BBC Russian Service and Mediazona said at least 7,421 foreigners have been killed fighting on Russia's side.Suicides, alcohol and drug use prevalentJournalists also analysed deaths among Russian servicemen from non-combat causes. Around 2,500 died as a result of alcohol and drug use or suicide.According to confidential Rosstat data analysed by the international news outlets, more than 1,000 Russian servicemen took their own lives since the start of the invasion.The deaths of another 885 soldiers in Ukraine or near its borders were registered as firearm injuries "with undetermined intent," a classification experts believe is used in some cases to conceal suicides.Together, the two figures represent a number comparable to a full Russian regiment.Military analysts note the problem is deepened in the Russian armed forces by intense pressure from fellow soldiers and commanders, fear of assignment to high-casualty fighting areas known as "meatgrinder assaults," and contracts that in practice prevent soldiers from leaving the war.Toll highest away from MoscowThe number of Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine is the highest in Russia's Far East and Siberia relative to their populations.Russia's Jewish Autonomous Region in the Far East recorded nearly 1,000 deaths per 100,000 inhabitants, Zabaykalsky around 800, Chukotka 760 and Tuva 650.Moscow, which the authorities have worked to insulate from the visible effects of the war, recorded 63 deaths per 100,000 inhabitants, according to Important Stories.The Kremlin does not publish or recognise figures for Russian losses from the invasion. Russian authorities have restricted access to official databases and prosecuted those conducting independent counts.Ukraine's General Staff estimated Russia's losses since February 2022 at 1,639,641 servicemen, encompassing both killed and wounded, although the figure has not been independently verified.The Economist, in a study published at the end of October, put the number of Russian servicemen killed at between 374,000 and 770,000, and total losses including the wounded at between 1.4 and 2.1 million.The Ukrainian armed forces' General Staff reported that October of this year was the bloodiest month for Russia since the invasion began.The Insider said the Russian armed forces suffered their heaviest losses in spring 2025, during fighting on the Pokrovsk axis, when more than 61,000 were killed over three months.
